texts: good. every participant lands — the gust of wind, the lantern it put out, the Middle Row as the lantern's position, the evening, and the past tense. One caveat on our side rather than yours: "day 410 of Year 2" is stored with the same day term we use for a day-of-month, so it reads as day-of-month 410; no rewrite of yours avoids that, so keep the sentence as written.
good. the seeing, Marra as the perceiver, the gust as what she saw and her station as the vantage point are all covered, and the gust correctly reuses the symbol introduced in the first sentence.
good. the walk, Marra as the walker, and the same lantern as her destination are all covered.

mixed: the relighting itself is fully covered — Marra as agent, the same lantern, past tense, and the "re-" of "relit" recorded as a repetition tag — but "within the hour" is dropped, because we have no head for a forward time-window, so nothing in the parse bounds how soon she relit it. If the promptness matters downstream, state it as a measured gap from an already-named event instead: "Marra Tallowhand relit the lantern one hour after the gust." Note that this stores an exact one-hour gap rather than an upper bound, so if "no more than an hour" is the point, leave the sentence as written and accept the loss.
good. the denial is stored as a negated position of the lantern at the Sunken Cove, with the cove's name and kind kept outside the denial so they stand as facts — exactly the right shape.

good. this is stored as the denial that any wraith emerged, which is the faithful reading for a dated one-off narrative; the surface word "no" gets no separate carrier of its own, but nothing in the claim is lost.

bad: "recorded the incident as a minor weather event" loses the direct object — the classification takes the slot the incident should occupy, so "what did the Council record?" binds nothing — and the as-phrase has no licensed form of its own, so it should not be sitting there at all. Rewrite it as a finite clause, which makes the classification the thing recorded and is a shape we handle cleanly: "The Council recorded that the incident was a minor weather event." Separately, "the incident" as a summary label for the whole episode mints a fresh thing that is not tied back to the extinguishing; if you need that link, re-mention the event rather than summarizing it.

good. the recommendation seals correctly — the Council's issuing, the extra mire-essence, the Cliff Path lantern group and the per-lantern "wind-exposed" restriction all sit inside what was recommended, while the lantern group, the Cliff Path name and the mire-essence genus stand outside as facts.
good. "took the recommendation under advisement" is kept whole as one idiom, with the Council as the actor and the earlier recommending event correctly reused as what was taken up.
